title: Thermal threshold hopping & fairshare probe — incident notes and runbook sketch
content:
Summary:
This doc captures the post-incident capture and an early runbook sketch for a class of degradation we saw on Dedicated GPU pools where the hosts briefly \"therm-hop\" (thermal sensor hysteresis causes repeated clock/frequency scaling) while the fairshare allocator simultaneously reshuffles slots, producing amplified latency and sporadic request failures. Felt different from classic noisy-tenant eviction: root appears to be short thermal excursions + aggressive fairshare rebalancing during the same time window.

Why this matters:
- Customers observed token-level latency spikes (p50 -> p99) and a handful of generation failures when their workloads got rescheduled mid-KV-cache warmup.
- Autoscaler reacted to apparent throughput drops and started provisioning/evicting, which made the oscillation worse.
- Short-lived (1–8 minutes) but high-impact: user-visible errors and SLO alerts.

What we observed (signal timeline):
- 02:13 UTC — first latency spike on regional pool eu-west2-dedicated-a (alerts from synthetic tests).
- 02:14–02:18 UTC — rapid per-host frequency downward steps in telemetry: clocks.sm and clocks.gr drop intermittently across 6 hosts. Temperature sensors report 84–88C peaks then fall 6–10C as fans ramp.
- 02:15 UTC — fairshare controller emits reschedule events (slot migration) for tenants A, B, C to consolidate load; migrations complete at 02:17.
- 02:16 UTC — KV cache warmup broken by migration, token generation latency skyrockets for affected tenants.
- 02:18 UTC — autoscaler interprets tenant throughput drop and triggers extra slot creation; some slots start on different hardware, KV caches cold.
- 02:22 UTC — system stabilizes after thermal ramp-down and throttling stops; latency returns to baseline.

Immediate mitigations performed during incident:
- Temporarily increased thermal margin in host-level power profile for eu-west2 pool (ops-config PR #412) to reduce frequency hopping (manual patch rolled to ~20% of hosts as canary).
- Paused fairshare defrag/reschedule job for 10m to avoid concurrent migrations while thermal conditions were unsettled.
- Pinned heavy-IO tenants to existing slots for the duration of the spike (tenant-level override).
- Adjusted autoscaler cooldown to 3m (was 30s) for the pool to avoid creating new slots while KV caches were cold.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Thermal hysteresis + power-limiting on certain host firmware versions causes rapid clock stepping under bursty load, which causes performance variability until fans stabilize.
2) Fairshare defragmentation / consolidation algorithm aggressively migrates slots when it sees transient throughput dips, making KV warm caches get invalidated and increasing tail latency.
3) Autoscaler sensitivity compounds the oscillation by creating slots mid-event; new slots don't help until caches warm and cause further pressure.

Evidence supporting hypotheses:
- Correlation between clock reductions (clocks.* telemetry) and reschedule events within a 30s window for the same hosts.
- Host-level telemetry shows repeated temperature climbs that coincide with the frequency drops — indicates hardware-level thermal throttling rather than user workload change alone.
- Configurable fairshare logs show defragmentation heuristics triggered by perceived imbalance (short-lived), and the heuristics do not require sustained signal — they run on ephemeral windows.

Runbook sketch — immediate steps (for oncall):
1) Identify affected hosts quickly:
   - kubectl -n infra get pods -l pool=dedicated-eu-west2 -o wide  (or internal host lookup)
   - run: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,clocks.sm,clocks.mem --format=csv -l 1 on suspect nodes (via ssh)
   - flag hosts with temperature > 82C + repeated clock drops as "therm-hopping"
2) Short-circuit automated reshuffle / defrag:
   - disable the fairshare defrag job: /ops/fairshare/defrag disable --pool eu-west2-dedicated --reason \"therm-hop active\"
   - set a 10m hold on slot migrations for affected pool (control-plane toggle)
3) Increase thermal headroom (soft) on affected hosts (canary first):
   - roll ops-config thermal_profile: \"conservative\" -> increases fan curve / lowers target clock ceiling
   - apply to one rack first, monitor clocks/temps for 5–10m before broader rollout
4) Harden autoscaler sensitivity temporarily:
   - double cooldown and require 2 sequential low-throughput windows before adding slots
   - revert after stability for 15m
5) Evacuate the hottest 1–2 hosts if thermal oscillation persists:
   - cordon node, migrate non-latency-critical tenants off first
   - use maintenance drain with KV-preserve annotations where possible
6) Post-incident: create a job to replay the event in staging with targeted thermal stress tests + fairshare toggles.

Runbook sketch — longer-term actions / experiments to validate:
- Add a short preflight check in fairshare defrag that looks for host thermal/clock instability; if instability observed, skip defrag for 15m.
- Add a hysteresis window to autoscaler to require sustained low-throughput (2 consecutive 1m windows) before creating slots for dedicated pools.
- Investigate firmware rollbacks / BIOS settings for affected host models; coordinate with capacity ops.
- Implement a per-host thermal health metric that marks a host as \"avoid-migrate\" until stable for X minutes.
- Explore soft-power capping for tenants (per-tenant max power draw) for heavy models to limit thermal edge cases.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did only a subset of hosts exhibit therm-hopping? (possible firmware/SMBIOS difference or rack-level airflow differences)
- What is the interaction between fan controller vs firmware-level power limiting? Need vendor docs and test hardware.
- Would preemptive warming (gradual ramp) of KV caches for migrating slots avoid the worst spikes, or is the migration cost still too high?
- Is there a workload fingerprint (IO-heavy vs memory-bound) that correlates strongly with triggering therm-hops?

Postmortem action items (owner, ETA):
- ops-config: add thermal_profile conservative option and test across 3 racks (owner: Jorge Ramos, ETA: 2024-11-17)
- fairshare: add thermal-check gate before defrag (owner: Ava Chen, ETA: 2024-11-24)
- autoscaler: introduce 2-window confirmation for slot creation for dedicated pools (owner: Liam O'Neill, ETA: 2024-11-21)
- capacity: audit firmware revisions on hosts in eu-west2 and flag anomalies (owner: Priya Singh, ETA: 2024-11-14)
- SRE: create synthetic test harness to reproduce therm-hop + migration interplay in staging (owner: Maya Patel, ETA: 2024-11-30)

Notes-to-self / talk tracks for post-incident sync:
- We should avoid calling this purely a \"noisy-tenant\" incident in customer comms — the amplification path was operational (defrag + autoscale) interacting with hardware thermal behaviour.
- For customers: explain we reduced noise by pausing consolidation and tuning autoscaler; long-term fixes involve scheduling and host firmware/thermal profiles.
- Consider an A/B test of a \"migration-safety\" flag for heavy workloads so enterprise customers can opt-out of live consolidation if they prefer stability over consolidation.

Immediate follow-up actions I did after incident:
- Opened SRE-1247 with telemetry snippets and preliminary hypothesis.
- Rolled conservative thermal_profile to 2 hosts as canary (ops-config PR #412).
- Temporarily paused fairshare defrag for eu-west2 for 1h while we monitored.

Appendix — useful commands and logs to collect quickly:
- list active migrations: opsctl fairshare list-migrations --pool eu-west2-dedicated --since 5m
- host telemetry quickdump: curl -s http://telemetry.internal/api/hosts?pool=eu-west2-dedicated&since=10m | jq '.[] | {host,temps,clocks,event_counts}'
- nvidia-smi live sampling: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,clocks.sm,clocks.mem --format=csv -l 1
- autoscaler history: opsctl autoscaler history --pool eu-west2-dedicated --window 30m

Unresolved items (for next sync):
- Confirm whether fan-control profile changes require host reboot / disruption.
- Determine safe default for autoscaler cooldown for all dedicated pools (global policy?).
- Decide on customer opt-out UX for live consolidation.

If you're oncall and see this pattern: prioritize pausing consolidations and stabilizing thermal environment before letting autoscaler / defrag run. Avoid knee-jerk slot creation while KV caches are actively being invalidated.

End of notes.
